conviction_note: The evidence is close to balanced. On the positive side, the quarter's components that management guided imply Q3 revenue of about $226-229M against a $225.2M consensus, and the CEO bought $1.0M of stock ten weeks into the quarter. On the negative side, the full-year guide needs a record Q4 (about $250M total, about $26.5M EOS after $19M in Q3) at a company that cut its EOS guide in May and fell 32%, and the stock has run +22.5% in 20 days into a print whose in-line predecessor sold off 7.5%. So p_up 49 on an 11.5% absolute move; the -1.0 findings sum and the -0.23 scaled number agree in sign.

findings.finding: Adding up management's own Q3 components gives about $226-229M of Q3 revenue against a $225.2M consensus, roughly 0.5-1.5% above the bar and inside the FY guide. The components: H2 surgical revenue growth guided at ~18% on high-teens case volume growth with revenue per case down ~2.7%, applied to Q3'25 surgical of $177M, gives $207-209M; Q3 EOS was guided to ~$19M at the Wells Fargo conference in September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-04): revenue $213.5M against $211.3M est (+1%), EBITDA guide raised, stock -7.54%. Q3 2025: beat and raise, +16.29%. Q1 2026: revenue miss ($192M against $197.5M) plus EOS cut, -31.67%. A small in-line beat has been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $225.2M implies surgical growth of about 16-17%, below the ~18% H2 surgical growth management guided. If the market had taken the guided components literally, estimates would sit at $227-229M. The gap is small and inside the guide, so it is mostly a confirmation that the bar is reachable, not a surprise.
findings.independence: Q3'25 base (surgical $177M, EOS $20M): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350653/000119312525258609/atec-ex99_1.htm. H2 surgical ~18% and high-teens volume: Q2 call transcript, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/alphatec-atec-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/. Both are company statements, so this is one company source read twice, not independent corroboration.

findings.finding: CEO Patrick Miles bought 115,000 shares in the open market on 2026-09-10 at an average $8.81 ($1.01M), about 10 weeks into Q3 and after July and August trends were known to him. Form 4 filed 2026-09-11. It is the only open-market insider purchase found in 2026; the other 2026 insider activity is sales and grants.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy-into-print instance found for this name. In March 2026 insiders were sellers (COO Lish sold 260,535 shares, per InsiderTrades), and the Q1 print that followed fell 31.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is up ~38% since the purchase, so the market has already read part of the insider signal. If it were fully priced, the run-up would carry a matching estimate revision, and consensus revenue ($225M) has not moved above the guided path.
findings.independence: Purchase details: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-alphatec-nasdaq-atec-shares-up-51-still-a-buy-2026-10-28/ (same Form 4, not independent). Management's reaffirmation of FY targets on the same date (Wells Fargo conference, 2026-09-10) points the same way.

findings.finding: The reaffirmed FY guide is back-end loaded into Q4, which raises the risk of a trim on the call. With Q1 $192.1M, Q2 $213.5M and a ~$226M Q3, the $882M FY guide needs Q4 of about $250M (+17.6% against Q4'25 $213M), while H1 grew 14.4%. EOS is the sharpest piece: $77M FY less Q1 $14M, Q2 $17.5M and Q3 ~$19M leaves ~$26.5M for Q4, +40% sequential. EOS was cut from $85M to $77M in May on installation timing, and that print fell 31.7%. The finding is sized net of surgical (~91% of revenue), which is guided to grow, so a modest EOS-only trim is the main case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026: EOS guide cut $85M to $77M plus Q1 miss, -31.67%. January 2026: preliminary 2025 and 2026 outlook ($890M), -22.34%. August 2026: total revenue guide reaffirmed and EBITDA raised, -7.54%. This name has not paid for guidance holds and has punished cuts hard.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side ratings are 13 of 15 Buy, and the stock ran +22.5% in 20 days on no company news, which is not how a market that expected a guide trim would trade. If a cut were expected, consensus Q4 and FY would sit below $882M; aggregators show the FY guide as the anchor.
findings.independence: Q3 EOS $19M and the 'stronger order book' claim: https://www.getmidas.com/midasin-kulaklari/alphatec-wells-fargo-konferansinda-2026-hedeflerini-korudugunu-acikladi-p-742032. The May EOS cut: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ATEC/21165. The counterweight is management's September statement of a stronger EOS order book, which is why the size is small.

findings.finding: Elective surgery was soft in hospital data for Q3 2026. HCA (reported 2026-10-27): same-facility inpatient surgeries -1.4% YoY, outpatient surgeries -3.7%, ASC surgeries -5.4%, which management attributed to exchange-coverage losses. ATEC said on its Q2 call that ACA exposure is under 5% of its volume, so the transmission is weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HCA's Q2 2026 surgical volumes were weaker still (inpatient -2.3%, outpatient -4.4%), and ATEC still printed 20% case volume growth in Q2. The macro surgical series has not shown up in ATEC's volumes.
findings.why_not_priced: Released two days before the print, after ATEC last spoke. ATEC's run-up into the print shows no read-across, but ATEC's own disclosure (ACA under 5%) gives a reason for that.
findings.independence: Proxy only. HCA's own release: https://s23.q4cdn.com/949900249/files/content_files/FINAL-PR_HCA-Reports-3Q-2026-Results.pdf (same company, one fact). ATEC's ACA under 5% (Q2 call, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/alphatec-atec-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) argues against it.

findings.finding: J&J's fiscal Q3 2026 10-Q says Spine, Sports & Other growth was 'partially offset by competitive pressures and inventory dynamics', and Orthopaedics overall grew 3.4% operationally. That is a large incumbent saying it is losing spine share in the quarter ATEC is reporting, consistent with ATEC's share-gain story (ATEC's H1 volume was +20% against a low-single-digit market).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of ATEC reacting to J&J spine commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: J&J spine is buried in a combined franchise line with no number, so no aggregator turns it into a read-through. Globus (Nov 5) and Medtronic report after the window, so this is the only large spine incumbent to have spoken.
findings.independence: Proxy. Globus Q2 2026 US Spine slowed to +7% from ~10% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001237831/000162828026054353/gmed-q22026ex991.htm), also consistent with ATEC taking share, but that was Q2.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print +22.5% over 20 days, +6.8% over 5 days and ~+38% from the September low ($8.81), with no company news. On 2026-10-28 it rose 5.1% on volume 85% below average. Of the last three prints, the in-line one (Q2) still fell 7.5%. Short interest of 9.9% of float, falling, limits squeeze fuel either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 in-line beat and EBITDA raise sold -7.54%. Q4 2025 (Feb 2026): +0.79%. The baseline's last three prints were all flat or negative.
findings.why_not_priced: This is about what is priced, not an unpriced fact. The rally has lifted the bar without lifting estimates, so an in-line print now meets a stock that has already re-rated. If the run-up had come with revisions, consensus would sit above the ~$226M guided path.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew reading. The run-up (+22.5% over 20 days) and the history of selling in-line prints cut against the mildly positive reported-quarter findings, and the guide-risk finding agrees with the run-up having raised the bar. Net, the evidence sits near the middle, hence p_up 49.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): finding 1 lands inside guided components, so cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 5 (proxy, not a company number) and partial pricing after a +38% move: CEO-buy finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): EOS guide-trim risk sized net of guided surgical growth, -1.5 to -1.3
Rule 3/5 (own caveat; company document contradicts the transmission): HCA proxy cut from -0.3 to -0.2 because ATEC states ACA exposure under 5%; J&J proxy cut from +0.3 to +0.2
Rule 7 (short interest checked; 9.9% float, falling, not crowded): run-up negative shrunk from -0.8 to -0.6
Net: the findings sum is unchanged at -1.0 by coincidence of offsetting cuts; p_up moved from 50 to 49
